ambiguities.evidence: Definition 2.5.6 defines the norm as an infimum over positive scales, so the identically zero random variable has infimum 0, while Equation (2.14) nevertheless states the formula for all t >= 0 without a separate zero-norm convention.
ambiguities.impact: A fully literal formal statement may need an explicit convention or a separate treatment of the degenerate zero-norm case, especially at t = 0; that choice should not otherwise change the stated universal tail bound.
ambiguities.issue: The displayed quotient is not explicitly interpreted when ||X||_{psi_2} = 0.

contract_plain_english: There is a universal numerical constant c > 0 such that every sub-gaussian random variable has Gaussian-type two-sided tails: at every nonnegative threshold t, the chance that |X| reaches t is at most 2 exp(-c t^2 / ||X||_{psi_2}^2). The psi_2 norm is the exponential-square integrability scale defined in (2.13), and the source says this scale is optimal for the inequality up to universal constant factors.

source_evidence.observation: A random variable is called sub-gaussian when it satisfies any of the equivalent properties (i)--(iv) of Proposition 2.5.2, and its sub-gaussian norm is defined by ||X||_{psi_2} = inf {s > 0 : E exp(X^2/s^2) <= 2}.

source_evidence.anchor: Equation (2.14), in the paragraph beginning 'Let us restate Proposition 2.5.2'
source_evidence.observation: Every sub-gaussian random variable X satisfies P{|X| >= t} <= 2 exp(-c t^2 / ||X||_{psi_2}^2) for all t >= 0.
The source declares C and c to be positive absolute constants and says that, up to absolute constant factors, ||X||_{psi_2} is the smallest possible number making each displayed inequality valid.

binders: There is a positive absolute constant c.
X ranges over sub-gaussian real-valued random variables.
t ranges over real numbers with t >= 0.
definitions_and_conventions: Sub-gaussian means satisfying one (equivalently, every one) of properties (i)--(iv) in Proposition 2.5.2.
The event is the two-sided tail event {|X| >= t}.
The constant c is absolute: it is universal rather than depending on X or t.
hypotheses: X is sub-gaussian in the sense of Definition 2.5.6.
implicit_context: Probability P and expectation E are taken with respect to the probability law of X.
No centering or independence assumption is imposed for Equation (2.14).
The claim is a restatement of the equivalences in Proposition 2.5.2 using the psi_2 norm.

details: One positive absolute constant c works uniformly for every sub-gaussian X and every t >= 0.
The bound is two-sided because the event uses |X|.
The threshold enters quadratically with a negative exponent.
The scale is the square of the psi_2 norm, and the multiplicative prefactor is exactly 2.
The source additionally characterizes ||X||_{psi_2}, up to absolute constant factors, as the smallest scale for which the tail inequality can hold.

undebatable_constraints: The subject is a sub-gaussian random variable X as defined immediately before the equation.
The inequality applies for every threshold t >= 0.
The probability event is {|X| >= t}, not a one-sided event.
c is positive and absolute, hence independent of X and t.
Equation (2.14) does not require X to have mean zero and does not require any independence hypothesis.
